problem_type: Docs autosync publication and CI contracts drift during fixed-PR migration
symptom: PR #640 Contracts fails at scripts/run-gates-contracts.node-test.mjs:186 because the workflow replaced create-pull-request with a handwritten gh publisher.
direct_cause: The implementation removed the v7 action while the existing contract still requires it, SHA-scoped branches and a CI skip marker.
class_root: The single publication boundary and both workflow contracts did not migrate together to the approved fixed-branch/default-token behavior.
affected_population: Every main push requiring index/status/ledger repair
Manual repair reruns and updates to already-open repair PRs

external_sources.purpose: Default token recursion protection and explicit dispatch exception
Official independent App/PAT requirement for unapproved automated PR CI
Restore official v7 fixed-branch creation/update/no-diff lifecycle per user decision.

invariants: One create-pull-request@v7 publisher targets fixed docs/autosync against main without branch-suffix.
Both automatic pushes and manual reruns regenerate docs and pass the three docs gates before publication.
GITHUB_TOKEN owns publication with contents and pull-requests write; no dedicated secret, extra dispatch, CI skip markers or protected-main push.
Only docs changes are committed; action owns generated-branch lifecycle.
generality_proof: Both triggers converge on one serialized action publisher. The gates-chain test checks the approved action, fixed branch and no skip markers; the workflow tests check parsed permissions, scope, trigger and fail-before-publication boundaries. No parallel shell publisher remains.

shared_boundaries.responsibility: Publish only verified docs repairs using the upstream fixed-branch action and default token.

same_class_entry_points.evidence: Every main push uses the common serialized autosync job.
Manual retry uses the same repair, fail-closed gates and action publication as main pushes.

recurrence.reason: Every future main push or manual rerun can exercise a drifting publication contract; SHA-scoped publication previously produced seven blocked PRs.
same_class_scan: Inspected .github/workflows/docs-autosync.yml automatic push and manual dispatch entries, scripts/run-gates-contracts.node-test.mjs and docs/fixes/docs-autosync.node-test.mjs consumers.
Searched .github/workflows for create-pull-request, DOCS_AUTOSYNC_TOKEN, gh pr create and CI skip markers; SEO Radar already uses v7 fixed branch; download-stats writes a non-PR data branch.

prevention.invariant: Every docs repair uses one upstream fixed-branch action after successful docs gates, without suppressing CI.
prevention.failure_mode: Repair gate or action failure fails the job; workflow-contract regression fails Contracts.
prevention.strategy: Remove hand-written Git/gh publishing and credential branching; restore one upstream lifecycle for both entry points with default-token recursion protection.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove the hand-written gh/Git publisher and dedicated-token guard; SHA-suffixed branches and CI skip markers remain forbidden.

dependency_lifecycle.rationale: User explicitly selects v7 and the repository already uses it for SEO Radar. Retain the official fixed-branch lifecycle instead of implementing another publisher.
dependency_lifecycle.target: Official supported action version preserving the fixed-branch interface and GITHUB_TOKEN contract
exit_criteria: Upgrade when v7 is unsupported or a relevant security/compatibility fix requires a newer supported release; update the action assertion and rerun workflow contracts together.

migration: Reuse docs/autosync and its existing PR #642; remove the DOCS_AUTOSYNC_TOKEN requirement. Preserve historical cleanup receipts without changing other PRs. Update both current contracts to the approved shape in the same change.
residual_risks: GITHUB_TOKEN-created PR workflows may require maintainer approval under current official semantics; repairing #640 CI does not certify unattended generated-PR CI.
Action publication still depends on repository settings allowing GitHub Actions to create pull requests.
The v7 remote lifecycle is provided by upstream; local workflow contracts do not execute hosted PR API writes.
